title: Connexions de Gauss-Manin et équations de Picard-Fuchs. Opération de Cartier : copies de tapuscrit annoté (s.d.), tiré à part (1981), notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Context (pp. 120-123). Grothendieck is studying the map from torsors of projective structures (H^1 P_{X/S}) to the sheaf of 'connections' Conn_{0,X/S}, a torsor under ω^{⊗2}. In characteristic p he expects a statement of Cartier type: with O'_X the subsheaf of functions killed by D^(i) for i ≤ 3 (which is O^(p) for p ≠ 2,3, and O^(p^2) otherwise), the map H^1_{X^{(p)}/S} P_{X/S} → Conn_0 should be injective. This needs a local lemma, stated on p.121.

Lemma (p.121). Let A be a local ring of characteristic p > 3, α ∈ A, B = A[T]/(T^p − α), and t the class of T. Put D^(i) = (1/i!)(d/dt)^i for i ≤ 3. The normalized Schwarzian is c_0(s) = −D^(3)s/D^(1)s + (D^(2)s/D^(1)s)^2, defined when D^(1)s ∈ B^*. Since S(s) = s'''/s' − (3/2)(s''/s')^2 = 6(D3/D1 − (D2/D1)^2), we have c_0 = −S/6, consistent with the 1/12 normalization on p.120. Claim: c_0(s) = 0, i.e. (D^(2)s)^2 = D^(1)s · D^(3)s, holds iff s = (at+b)/(ct+d) with a,b,c,d ∈ A, ad − bc = 1, unique up to a scalar unit.

This page proves the key case.

1. Reduction to α = 0. One may assume α ∈ A^p, presumably by faithfully flat extension adjoining α^{1/p}. Translating t by α^{1/p} then gives α = 0, so t is nilpotent (t^p = 0). Writing s = Σ a_i t^i, we get D^(1)s ≡ a_1 mod t, so D^(1)s is a unit iff a_1 ∈ A^*.

2. First normalization. Replacing s by a_1^{-1}(s − a_0), an affine Möbius map, gives s = t + a_2 t^2 + ….

3. Second normalization. Apply s ↦ s/(1 + a_2 s) = Σ_{n≥0} (−1)^n a_2^n s^{n+1}. Here 1 + a_2 s is a unit because s is nilpotent. The result is s ≡ t mod t^3. Both changes are Möbius, and the Schwarzian is invariant under post-composition by Möbius maps, so c_0 = 0 is preserved.

4. Induction. It remains to show that s = t + a t^d + O(t^{d+1}) with 3 ≤ d ≤ p−1 and c_0(s) = 0 forces a = 0. Modulo t^{d−2}:
- D^(3)s ≡ a·C(d,3)·t^{d−3};
- D^(2)s ≡ 0;
- D^(1)s ≡ 1.
Hence a·C(d,3)·t^{d−3} ≡ 0 mod t^{d−2}. Since B is A-free on 1, t, …, t^{p−1} and d−3 < p, this gives C(d,3)·a = 0. Now 6 is invertible (p > 3), and d(d−1)(d−2) is invertible because 3 ≤ d ≤ p−1. So a = 0.

Iterating up to t^{p−1} gives s = t. Undoing the normalizations, the original s is a Möbius transform of t with coefficients in A.

The next page treats p = 2, 3. There one needs B = A[T]/(T^{p^2} − α) with divided-power derivatives, and checks via Lucas' theorem that C(d,3) ≠ 0 in F_p for 3 ≤ d ≤ p^2 − 1.

Meaning: in characteristic p, the local solutions of the Schwarzian equation S(s) = 0 are exactly the PGL_2(O^p)-orbit of a coordinate t, or PGL_2(O^{p^2}) when p = 2, 3. This is a local 'Cartier theorem' for projective structures.
errors: No real error in the p>3 argument. The reduction 'OPS α ∈ A^p' needs a faithfully flat base change A → A[α^{1/p}]. Returning to A then needs descent of the Möbius matrix: the scalar-unit uniqueness gives descent to PGL_2, and lifting to SL_2 needs the hypothesis ₂Pic(A) = 0 added on p.121. This step is not written out on this page.
Implicit: Möbius invariance of c_0 (the cocycle formula S(g∘f) = (S(g)∘f)·f'^2 + S(f)) is used without comment when normalizing by s/(1+a_2 s). It is valid here since only D^(i) for i ≤ 3 < p occur.
The 'il suffit' step should be read as an induction on d. After showing a = 0 for the lowest-order term, one proceeds to the next term. This is correct but not stated.

ideas.what: In char p > 3, a function s on the infinitesimal neighbourhood B = A[T]/(T^p) has vanishing Schwarzian iff s is a Möbius transform of t with coefficients in A, i.e. constants for d/dt = p-th powers. In char 2, 3 one must pass to level p^2 with divided powers.
ideas.modern_name: Kernel of the Schwarzian in positive characteristic; local structure of Frobenius-projective structures / dormant PGL_2-opers
ideas.usually_credited_to: Ihara (Schwarzian equations in char p, 1970s); Mochizuki (p-adic Teichmüller theory, dormant opers, 1990s); Hoshi, Wakabayashi (Frobenius-projective structures, 2010s)

ideas.what: Normalization of a coordinate change to s ≡ t mod t^3 via affine and Möbius maps, then order-by-order vanishing via C(d,3) ≠ 0 for 3 ≤ d ≤ p−1
ideas.modern_name: Standard jet normalization for Schwarzian/projective structures

ideas.what: Normalization c_0 = −S/6 with D^(i) = ∂^i/i!, so that the Schwarzian is expressed with divided-power derivatives (allowing an extension to char 2, 3 via higher divided powers)

missed.claim: Around 1972 Grothendieck formulates a Cartier-type theorem for projective structures. Its target is injectivity of H^1 with coefficients in X^{(p)} (torsors of projective coordinates modulo PGL_2(O^p)) into the torsor of projective connections Conn_0 (opers) under ω^{⊗2}. This page proves the local lemma: vanishing Schwarzian means Möbius over O^p, or O^{p^2} when p = 2, 3. This anticipates the 'Frobenius-projective structure' and dormant oper viewpoint of Mochizuki and Hoshi, here placed inside his Gauss–Manin/Cartier-operator project.
missed.quote: À prouver que sous ces conditions, la condition c_0(s)=0 ⇒ s=t
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: It shows an early, unpublished link by Grothendieck between Cartier's operator and the char-p Schwarzian / projective connections. The literature attributes this circle of ideas to Ihara and Mochizuki. The special treatment of p = 2, 3 via O^{p^2} matches later work on Frobenius-projective structures of level n.

deep.surprise_reason: The computation itself is elementary. The context is a char-p Cartier theorem for projective structures with the p = 2, 3 refinement at level p^2, which is an unpublished precursor of later work (Ihara, Mochizuki, Hoshi). That is a notable historical detail, though plausibly 'folklore-level' for specialists.
transcription_corrections: 'puis α ≠ 0' should read 'puis α = 0': after reducing to α ∈ A^p and translating t, one gets t^p = 0. The symbol is a struck-through/overwritten '='.
'dans t ∈ tB' is more likely 'donc t ∈ rad B' (t nilpotent), which is consistent with D^(1)s ≡ a_1 mod t giving the unit criterion.
In the D^(1)s line the struck text is '+ a d t^{d-1}', i.e. the derivative term; the modulus is t^{d-1}.
